prompts.organize:
You organise a parent's notes about their child, {name}, into passport entries that help other carers understand {name}.
Rules:
- Use ONLY facts stated in the NOTES. Never add advice, guesses or facts of your own.
- Make one entry per distinct fact.
- section is one of: communication, calming, upsets, likes, pain, medical, routine, safety.
- signal: what a carer sees or hears, or the fact itself. At most 15 words.
- meaning: what it means. Fill it for communication and pain entries; otherwise use an empty string.
- whatToDo: what helps, only if the NOTES say so; otherwise an empty string.
- quote: copy 3 to 12 words EXACTLY, word for word, from the NOTES that support the entry.

NOTES:
"""
{notes}
"""
prompts.answer:
You help a carer look after {name}, a child who cannot easily explain themselves.
The carer says: "{question}"

These are the ONLY facts you may use, from {name}'s passport, written by the parent:
{facts}

Rules:
- Use only these facts. Never add medical advice or anything not in them.
- answer: at most 3 short, calm sentences (under 60 words) saying what it probably means and what the carer should do. Talk to the carer directly as "you". The parent is {parent}: if the carer should contact the parent, say "call {parent}", never "call me". Do not write ids in the answer.
- usedIds: the ids of the facts you used, for example ["e2"].
- found: "found" if the facts clearly answer it, "partial" if they help at all, "none" only if not one fact is related (then answer is an empty string). If any fact could help the carer right now, use it.
prompts.observation:
A carer noticed something new about {name}: "{observation}"

Current passport entries that may be related:
{facts}

Propose ONE passport change using only what the carer said.
- action: "add" for a new fact, or "edit" to improve an existing entry (then set editId to its id).
- section is one of: communication, calming, upsets, likes, pain, medical, routine, safety.
- signal, meaning and whatToDo follow the same meaning as the existing entries. Use empty strings for parts the carer did not say.

demo.note: A fictional child for demos and judges. No real child data.

child.aboutMe: Loves buses, trains and the colour yellow

entries.signal: Says "ba-ba" and points at the window
entries.meaning: He wants to watch the buses
entries.whatToDo: Let him watch for two minutes, then say "bus finished"
Give him a drink of water
Tell him Mum is coming. Call her if he keeps asking

entries.signal: Pulls your hand to the fridge
entries.whatToDo: Offer a snack. Banana slices are his favourite
This is fine, please do not stop him

entries.meaning: He is in pain, or it is too loud for him
entries.whatToDo: Take him somewhere quiet first. If he keeps doing it, call Mum: it may be an ear infection

entries.signal: Goes very quiet and lies on the floor
entries.whatToDo: Check if he feels hot and call Mum

entries.signal: Loud noises like hand dryers, blenders and fire alarms
entries.whatToDo: Move him away from the noise and speak softly
Tell him what is happening next before it happens

entries.signal: Someone touching his head or grabbing his arm
entries.whatToDo: Do not do this, he panics. Hold his hand gently instead
Hum it softly, close to him

entries.signal: A tight hug or a heavy blanket
entries.whatToDo: Use it when he is overwhelmed
Talk about buses to connect with him

entries.signal: The colour yellow and banana slices
entries.whatToDo: A yellow toy or banana slices cheer him up
His EpiPen is in the front pocket of his bag. If he reacts, use it and call the emergency number
If he stands by the door and rocks, he needs to go
Give him 20 minutes of quiet time

entries.signal: Runs off when he sees a bus or water
entries.whatToDo: Always hold his hand near roads. He does not understand traffic

entries.signal: Will not answer to his name if lost
entries.whatToDo: Speak softly, say "Sam, bus finished", and stay with him
